comment: What the editorial-author skill would decide for the demo article. '@<priority>:<n>' placeholders are resolved to author-input item ids by src/demo/editorial.ts.

default.rationale: Does not change how this particular story should be told.

body-conflict-early.rationale: The story has a real, evidenced conflict (ADR-0003, Context): the one-off audit could not tell a new finding from one already seen. Exposing it early costs nothing in accuracy.
body-conflict-early.consequence: Open on the noisy report that mixes new and already-seen findings; the first version's architecture comes after, as a link to the previous article.
safeguards: Do not dramatise: no invented incidents, only the behaviour documented in ADR-0003.

title-conflict.rationale: The title can name the concrete change (findings that persist between runs) without conflict framing that would overstate a routine design change.
title-conflict.consequence: Title names the subject and the change: the audit starts remembering findings.

body-technical-early.rationale: Code belongs to the lifecycle episode; putting it before the conflict would turn the opening into documentation.
body-technical-early.consequence: First code (the transition table) right after the conflict and the link back, not in the first paragraph.

body-code.rationale: Two short real snippets prove the lifecycle and the storage claims.
body-code.consequence: Show the transition table and the migration, nothing else.

body-measurements.rationale: There are no measurements; the story lists their absence as a limitation. Numbers cannot be added to follow a trend.

body-next-steps.rationale: The story has one open question and one labelled plan; a short closing is honest, a roadmap would not be.
body-next-steps.consequence: Close with the open question and the labelled future plan.

direction.readerPromise: Show how an audit that forgot everything between runs became a model that remembers findings, and what that memory costs.
direction.coreAngle: The architecture readers know from the previous article stopped fitting regular use; the story is what had to change for the tool to remember.
direction.primaryConflict: The one-off audit could not tell a new finding from one already seen and deliberately left.
secondaryThemes: SQLite as the price of memory
direction.openingApproach: Open on the noisy report (new and already-seen findings mixed) before any history; link the previous article in the second section.
direction.narrativeEmphasis: Dwell on the finding lifecycle; pass quickly over storage and the pipeline refactor.
direction.technicalDepth: High: the real transition table and migration; no invented numbers.
direction.personalDepth: Moderate: only the author's own note about why the overwritten report seemed fine.
direction.humorPolicy: One light joke from the author's material (the amnesiac audit); nothing else.
direction.codePolicy: Two short snippets that prove a point: the transition table and the migration.
direction.visualPolicy: The lifecycle code doubles as the visual; the before/after diagram is optional.

voicePlan.readerExperience: Not a description of the new architecture, but the moment a tool that forgot everything starts to remember, and the price of that memory.
voicePlan.conflictPlacement: First paragraph (beat report-noise), before any history.
delayedContext: How the first version worked (runner → rules → report) comes after the conflict, as a link to the previous article.
